# Golden files

These files are the gate in `docs/plans/HARNESS-PORTABILITY-PLAN.md` section 8.
A change to the importer or the reconciler merges only when its output matches
the golden, or the difference is an intended fix that ships its own test.

| File | Written by | Checked by |
|------|------------|------------|
| `importer-state.golden` | `SyncHarnessStats` on `testdata/memory`, dumped table by table | `internal/importer/golden_test.go`, `TestGoldenImportState` |
| `reconcile-dry-run.golden` | `scripts/reconcile-memory.py --dry-run` against a fake service | `scripts/test_reconcile_golden.py`, `ReconcileDryRunGolden` |

## Fixture cases

The shipped fixture carries the inputs for the reconciler's mission-ID and
step-status paths. Each is written in the Markdown shape Bishop writes. The
files are the source; this section does not list them.

- `findings/FINDINGS.md`: each fixture entry has a `**Mission**` field. Its
  Rationale says what the entry exercises.
- `state/MISSION-ARCHIVE.md`: the rows are the known mission ids the
  `**Mission**` fields are checked against. An id with no row here, and no
  folder under `missions/`, is not known.
- `missions/mission-20260904-01/PROGRESS.md`: a step row carries a status
  outside the step set.

Only existing files carry these cases. No file was added, because the
importer test asserts the exact document count. The importer golden embeds the
body of `findings/FINDINGS.md`, so an edit to that file changes it.

## Regenerating a golden

An intended change is recorded with update mode:

    UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 go test ./internal/importer -run TestGoldenImportState -count=1
    UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 python3 scripts/test_reconcile_golden.py

Update mode writes the file and then fails the test on purpose. Run the same
command again without `UPDATE_GOLDEN` to confirm. CI sets `UPDATE_GOLDEN` to the
empty string, so update mode never runs in CI. The tests fail on any mismatch
against the committed golden.

## What the goldens cannot see

- **Request payloads.** The reconciler golden records the method and path of
  each request the fake receives, not the body. A write's payload is not
  compared.
- **Nested mission files.** The fixture's mission folder holds flat files.
  A golden cannot kill a mutant that only changes behaviour for a deeper path.
- **Values the goldens do not read.** The goldens do not pin: `AgentsDir`
  (`internal/profile/profile.go:51`, read by `AgentsDirFor` in
  `internal/importer/agents.go:19`, which the Go golden does not call), the
  approver default `APPROVER_DEFAULT` in `scripts/reconcile-memory.py:102`
  (used at `:1146`), `DefaultHarness` (`internal/profile/profile.go:61`, read
  by `cmd/mcpd/main.go:98`), and `ReviewerRole` (`internal/profile/profile.go:60`,
  read by `internal/api/crew.go:206` and `internal/api/hud.go:193`). These are
  not on the paths the golden tests exercise, as read from their call
  sites. `APPROVER_DEFAULT` is now pinned by `ApproverDefaultTests` in
  `scripts/test_reconcile_units.py` and is mutation-tested below. `AgentsDir`,
  `DefaultHarness` and `ReviewerRole` are not, and are still unpinned.
- **Finding links and step status values.** The dry-run labels a finding by
  its date and target, and a step by its number, so a wrong `**Mission**` link
  does not appear in the golden. A finding or step that is warned appears as a
  WARN line on stderr and in the summary's "warned" count, so a warning that
  stops firing is visible; the value a step status was rejected for is in the
  WARN line. A dropped step row does appear, because its line is gone. The
  links are pinned by `FindingMissionLinkTests` and `FindingWarningTests`, and
  the step statuses by `StepStatusTests` and `StepWarningTests`, all in
  `scripts/test_reconcile_units.py`, which read the shipped fixture.
- **Journal paging.** The golden's fake never pages: it answers each
  flight-recorder GET with an empty array and no `has_more`, so the golden
  reads only the path a server that does not page takes. The paging path
  (`fetch_journal` in `scripts/reconcile-memory.py`) is pinned by
  `PagedJournalTests` and `PagedJournalExitTests` in
  `scripts/test_reconcile_units.py`, and the server's `offset` and `has_more`
  by `TestListFlightRecorderPaging` in `internal/api/flight_recorder_list_test.go`.

## Mutant record (DIR-017)

Rows here come from an earlier mission and from mission-20261020-03. The rows labelled `5c` and `5e` were planted by an earlier mission, against commit `7438933`. The `importer` and `profile` packages have not changed since `718cb7a`, so the Go rows that edit them still describe the code. The rows labelled `m3-step3` were planted at step 3 of mission-20261020-03, against commit `e75e97f`, where the reconciler is unchanged from `2658de2`. The Python rows that step 3 planted against `5798e4c` were re-run at step 4a and carry the label `4a`. The rows labelled `4a` were planted at step 4a of mission-20261020-03 against commit `a949470`, whose reconciler is the one committed at `aab9fb7`. The rows labelled `m3-step6a` were planted at step 6a of mission-20261020-03 against commit `1c7e815`. They cover the journal paging in `flight_recorder.go` and `reconcile-memory.py`, and every line number in them is read at that commit. The commits `e75e97f`, `5798e4c`, `a949470`, `aab9fb7` and `1c7e815` named in this paragraph are on the reconciler-integrity branch and are not on `main`; that branch was squashed into PR #9 (`1c4def9`), so the content is on `main` but these SHAs are not in its history.

Each mutant was planted alone, its killers run, and the file reverted.
Each reverted file was checked with `cmp` against a copy saved before planting.
The failure text is copied from the run logs, not retyped. Each Python edge is a test
method; each Go edge is a subtest.

The **Last run** column names the run. `5c` and `5e` are steps of the earlier
mission. `4a` and every `m3-step` label name a step of mission-20261020-03.

Quoted failure text is verbatim. unittest appends a message passed to an
assertion as ` : <msg>`. On a one-line assertion the message follows the
`AssertionError` text on that line. On a multi-line diff (`Lists differ`,
`Tuples differ`) the message is on the diff's last line, which is quoted after
the `AssertionError` line. Each quote is prefixed by its test. The golden quotes
are the summary and WARN lines of the golden diff, and the exception line where a
run crashed. The retired rows and the Go rows keep the text they were recorded with.

Every mutant names the property it discriminates and its mirror, the opposite
edge. A mirror is killed by a test whose failure text differs from its partner's.
Each row says whether its mirror edits the same line or a different one.

Notes on the `m3-step6a` rows. Each mutant was planted alone against the clean tree at commit `1c7e815`, its killers were run, and the file was restored and byte-compared with the copy saved before planting (`flight_recorder.go` and `reconcile-memory.py` both restored identical). The planting script saved a copy of the file before each edit, and refused to plant an edit whose text did not occur exactly once. Go killers ran as `go test -c` once per mutant, then the test binary once per subtest with `-test.count=1`; every subtest of `TestListFlightRecorderPaging` was run under every Go mutant, so a subtest left out of a row's kill text was live. Python killers ran `python3 -B -I scripts/test_reconcile_units.py -v`, which reports every test method separately, and the Golden verdict is from `python3 -B -I scripts/test_reconcile_golden.py` run under the same mutant. Where a quote is a multi-line diff, the quote is the `AssertionError` line and the diff's last line, as above. The Go quotes are whole `t.Errorf` lines.

GO-TIE and GO-TIE-MIRROR are told apart by their failure text. GO-TIE fails `tie order paged by two` and `tie order without offset`, the two subtests whose rows share `created_at`; GO-TIE-MIRROR fails only `created_at precedence`. Dropping the tie-break altogether (`ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT ? OFFSET ?`) was also run: on this table SQLite then returns equal `created_at` rows in rowid order, so it fails the same two subtests with the same text as GO-TIE and is not a separate row.

Killed by methods outside the paging tests. PY-OLDCAP, PY-FAIL-FIRST and PY-PAGING-MIRROR are killed by `JournalCapTests` or `JournalCapExitTests` methods, and the rows name the killer quoted.

Golden. The golden's fake never pages. Each row says whether the golden is red or green under its mutant.

Notes on the record.

- **M2-mirror changed.** The previous mirror inverted the `isfile` test. That
  returns `[]` for a present file, the same output M2 gives, so the present-file
  test could not tell the two apart. The mirror now sits on the file-absent
  branch instead. This was reasoned from `parse_steps` and not run as the
  inversion; the sentinel mutant is the one that was run.
- **Shared kill lines in a mirror pair.** MUT-DIGITS2 and MUT-DIGITS3 quote the
  same lines: `AssertionError: '' != 'mission-20260907-anom-01'` and
  `AssertionError: None != 'mission-20260907-anom-01' : harness-qualified id: known id not carried in the create payload`.
  Both come from the anomaly id yielding no link under each mutant, because
  `anom` is not digits. The other quotes differ; the Observed failure column of
  each row names its killers.
- **MUT-LOOSE and MUT-THREE (retired) share a kill.** They are a mirror pair.
  Both fail the three-digit counter test with
  `'mission-20261009-100' != 'mission-20261009-10'`. That test has been renamed
  since `e75e97f`.
- **Shared lines outside a mirror pair.** M2 and SEAM-PY both fail
  `MissionsFolderLookupTests.test_declared_missions_folder_is_read` with the same
  line. Neither is the other's mirror, and each is told apart by a sibling test
  that stays green under the other: `StepTableTests.test_present_progress_yields_steps`
  stays green under SEAM-PY. SEAM-GO and SEAM-GO-LOOKUP share `importer_test.go:306`
  (Go, recorded at `7438933`).
- **Retired rows.** The rows marked `(retired)` are kept as they were observed on
  `e75e97f`, where they were run. Their edit targets, the old `MISSION_ID` pattern
  and the old `parse_steps` status line, were replaced at step 3, so they no
  longer apply. Their quotes carry the messages of the tests as they stood then,
  and they are not regenerated.
- **Same test method, distinct text.** MUT-NOLINK and MUT-ACCEPT both fail
  `FindingWarningTests.test_unknown_candidates_are_warned`, with `6 != 2` and
  `0 != 2`. MUT-WARN-SILENT and MUT-WARN-OVER both fail
  `StepWarningTests.test_unknown_status_is_warned_and_counted`, with `0 != 1`
  and `3 != 1`. The counts in the messages differ, so each path's text is its own.
  MUT-HYPHEN and MUT-SPACE-RUN, a mirror pair, both fail
  `FindingWarningTests.test_existing_unknown_candidate_is_not_warned`, and their
  quotes name different entries (`Harness-qualified id link` and
  `Trailing text link`).

M1-mirror and SEAM-PY-MIRROR pass the golden. That is the gap named under "What
the goldens cannot see". The unit tests carry those edges.

The rows marked `m3-step3 (e75e97f)` are the retired rows. They were run at step 3
of mission-20261020-03 against a clean export of commit `e75e97f`, taken with
`git archive`, and their edit targets no longer exist. The rows that step 3
planted against `5798e4c` were re-run as step 4a. Each run also ran the golden
test. A row whose observed failure says Golden green changes a link, a blanked
status or a cap count, which the dry-run does not print. A row that says Golden
red changes a line the dry-run does print.

## Layout values at the seam

The directory and file names the importer and the reconciler read are declared
once. The Go values are `profile.Bishop.Layout` in `internal/profile/profile.go`.
The Python values are `BISHOP_LAYOUT` in `scripts/reconcile-memory.py`.

Only the missions folder name has been checked, against the goldens and the
unit tests above. Changing it to `missionz` in each language fails the golden
and the lookup tests in that language (SEAM-GO and SEAM-PY above). No other
layout value is claimed as pinned; see "What the goldens cannot see" for the
values the goldens do not read.
